meta.method: WebSearch plus WebFetch, with maker PDFs downloaded by curl and read with pdftotext where WebFetch could not read them. confirmed:true means the figure was read on the cited page or file itself. confirmed:false means it came from a search-engine snippet or a secondary (dealer, review or aggregator) site, and the note says which. No figure was estimated. Where a figure could not be found, the entry says so and figure is null. Unit conversions are not given unless the source printed them.
caveats: Dealer pages and search snippets were used for many North American tow ratings because the makers' configurators are script-rendered. Those entries are confirmed:false.
Several Irish and UK spec sheets are undated or are launch-era documents. The note says so where that applies.

towing_guidance.item: Caravan and Motorhome Club: towcar matching ratio
towing_guidance.figure: 85% of the car's kerbweight for beginners; never exceed 100%
towing_guidance.note: Quoted: 'For optimum towing performance, we recommend to aim for a maximum towed load of no more than 85% of the car's kerbweight for beginners' ... 'Never exceed 100%.' The 85% applies to the caravan's laden weight (MTPLM).

towing_guidance.item: Camping and Caravanning Club: what can it tow
towing_guidance.figure: 85% of kerbweight target; up to 100% for experienced drivers, within the maker's towing limit
towing_guidance.note: Quoted: 'multiply it by 85/100. This will give you the important "85 per cent" figure.' and 'you can tow up to 100% of your car's kerbweight (as long as you don't exceed that all-important towing limit)', which the Club 'certainly wouldn't recommend ... for a beginner'. The Club says to compare against the caravan's MTPLM, the maker's towing limit, the plated train weight and the driving licence category. Both clubs say it is guidance, not law.

trailer_registration.item: New York State: trailer registration fee
trailer_registration.figure: $5.39 per 500 lb (or fraction) of maximum gross weight, annual, minimum $14.38, prorated daily, all expire 31 December. For 4,800 lb GVWR: 10 units x $5.39 = $53.90 per year.
trailer_registration.note: The rule is quoted from the page. The $53.90 is arithmetic on the published rule, not a figure printed by the DMV. The page says taxes and plate fees may also apply but gives no amount. Note that NY charges on maximum gross weight, not unladen weight.

trailer_registration.item: Connecticut: camp trailer registration (personal trailers, including travel trailers)
trailer_registration.figure: Registration fee $19 to $22.50 (depending on month registered); safety plate fee $5; title fee $25 plus $10 per lienholder if GVWR over 3,000 lb (and trailer under 29 years old); Passport to the Parks fee $24 from 1 July 2025 (was $15)
trailer_registration.note: Read from the page's HTML with curl, because WebFetch could not connect. Sales tax on registration is 6.35% (7.75% over $50,000). A 4,800 lb GVWR trailer is over 3,000 lb, so it needs a title.

trailer_registration.figure: Registration fee $76 (includes $3 alternative fuel/technology fee); CHP fee $34; Vehicle License Fee 0.65% of purchase price/value, declining over 11 renewal years. County and district fees vary.
trailer_registration.note: The page gives no trailer-coach-specific line. Trailer coaches pay VLF (per DMV handbook 3.075). Permanent Trailer Identification (PTI, $20 plus $10 every five years) applies to commercial and utility trailers, not trailer coaches. No total for a specific 4,800 lb trailer is published, because it depends on value.

trailer_registration.item: Great Britain: touring caravan registration and road tax (VED)
trailer_registration.figure: No domestic registration and no VED for a towed caravan. Since 26 August 2025, trailers over 750 kg must be registered with DVLA (£26 first registration) only to tow through or into most EU countries.
trailer_registration.publisher: GOV.UK (DVLA); Camping and Caravanning Club press release 2025
trailer_registration.note: GOV.UK quote: 'You must register all trailers over 750kg to drive through or to most countries in Europe apart from Ireland, Cyprus, Malta and Spain.' Fees: £26 first registration, £21 new keeper, £10 replacement. The 'no VED on caravans' point comes from secondary sources (Swift Group and others, unconfirmed on gov.uk), but VED applies to mechanically propelled vehicles, and towed caravans pay none.

trailer_registration.item: Ireland: caravan / light trailer registration and motor tax
trailer_registration.figure: Only trailers with design gross vehicle weight over 3,500 kg must be registered (first registration fee €60; annual licence renewal free with a roadworthiness certificate). A touring caravan under 3,500 kg needs no registration and pays no motor tax.
trailer_registration.note: The page states that trailers over 3,500 kg DGVW must be registered and that the fee is €60. That under-3,500 kg caravans are exempt follows from the threshold, but the page does not state it explicitly.
